sections.overview: This small-bodied rattlesnake is endemic to disjunct highland areas of central and southern Mexico.
sections.identification: Its distinctly small head and short, stout body distinguish it from many larger rattlesnakes.
sections.habitat: It occurs mainly in pine-oak highlands, but records also include cloud forest and dry habitats.
sections.diet: Museum stomach contents and earlier records point to Sceloporus lizards as its principal prey.
sections.behavior: This terrestrial snake shelters and forages among rocks; natural-history observations remain relatively sparse.
sections.reproduction: The species is live-bearing; published reports include a small litter, but reproductive data remain limited.
sections.ecology: It is a Mexican highland relative of Crotalus pusillus, though phylogenetic studies place them in different species groups.
sections.conservation: Its localized, fragmented range and narrow prey base make better field monitoring important for conservation.
